results.title: Switzerland vs Bosnia and Herzegovina FIFA World Cup 2026 Preview: Everything you need to know | Goal.com
highlights:
The upcoming clash in Southern California carries enormous implications as both nations look to solidify their knockout round ambitions in a highly balanced Group B layout. Taking place on the second matchday of the group stage, this encounter will inevitably be shaped by the immediate physical toll and psychological momentum of their opening fixtures. With the luxury of initial adjustments behind them, both camps head to the coast knowing that the margin for error has shrunk drastically, making tactical clarity absolute paramount.
[...]
Long-standing Switzerland head coach Murat Yakin has established a highly consistent, drama-free environment built to navigate these high-stakes tournament rhythms, relying on an experienced core designed to control midfield dynamics and absorb pressure. Standing across from them is a structurally resilient, emotionally charged Bosnia and Herzegovina side guided by Sergej Barbarez. Having remarkably eliminated Italy in the European play-offs, the Zmajevi possess an unyielding defensive blueprint and a dangerous mental edge that makes them incredibly stubborn opponents when elite structural discipline is demanded. Staged at the state-of-the-art Los Angeles Stadium (SoFi Stadium), the spectacular venue and its electric atmosphere will provide a fitting backdrop for a match where fine tactical margins will dictate the group's trajectory.
[...]
Switzerland go into this match with a mixed recent record across five games, posting two wins, two draws, and one defeat. Their most recent outing ended in a 1-1 draw with Australia on June 6, while their best result in the run was a 4-1 win over Jordan on May 31. They did suffer a 4-3 defeat to Germany in March, a match that exposed some defensive vulnerability. Across the five fixtures, Switzerland scored seven goals and conceded seven.
[...]
Bosnia and Herzegovina have gone four matches without a win in their last five, recording one win, three draws, and one defeat. Their most recent result was a 1-1 draw with Panama on June 6. Their sole win in the sequence came against Italy in World Cup qualifying back in March — a 1-1 draw that counted as a victory on aggregate — and they also beat Wales 1-1 on the same basis. Bosnia scored four goals and conceded four across their last five matches.

results.title: Haiti vs Scotland Predictions, Picks & Odds — Saturday, June 13 World Cup Match
highlights:
With a single win potentially enough to reach the knockout phase, the stakes are huge as Haiti and Scotland face off in Group C on Day 3 of the 2026 World Cup.
[...]
I expect a high-scoring affair between well-matched sides. Read on for my Haiti vs. Scotland predictions and key World Cup picks for Saturday, June 13.
[...]
## Who will win Haiti vs Scotland: Draw (+330)
[...]
The gap in quality between the teams is narrower than the market suggests. Outsiders Haiti’s starting lineup includes two English Premier League players (midfielder Jean-Jacques Bellegarde and striker Wilson Isidor) plus plenty of performers that have done well in France’s top two divisions down the years (Johnny Placide, Carlens Arcus, Jean-Kevin Duverne, Josue Casimir).
[...]
As favorites, Scotland are under pressure to start with three points before theoretically tougher upcoming fixtures against Morocco and Brazil. They head into the game in good form (6-1-3 in 10 2025/26 fixtures) and will enjoy good support at Boston Stadium.
[...]
Still, the expectations will weigh heavily on Scotland manager Steve Clarke and his players during the match as Haiti — way down the World Cup odds listings — refuse to simply stand aside.
[...]
Haiti +1.5 (-186) on the spread would be one way to support the dogs. If, like me, you would prefer a higher price, back things to stay level at +330.
[...]
## TOp pickHaiti vs Scotland Over/Under Pick: Over 2.5 (-109)
[...]
For both teams, attacks are better than defenses. The stats bear this out: six of Scotland’s last eight fixtures have had 3+ goals, for a high average of 3.63 goals per game.
[...]
Over 2.5 has landed in eight of Haiti’s 15 fixtures since June last year. The 4-4-2 formation they're expected to use encourages fast, vertical, attacking play, and can leave their defense exposed at the other end of the field.
[...]
All four pre-tournament friendlies involving Haiti and Scotland had 3+ goals (an average of 4.0 goals per game). Anybody watching those fixtures would have noted defensive flaws across both line-ups, with little time to correct them before this tournament opener.
[...]
This is the most winnable group game for both teams, so an open encounter - where the focus will be on winning, rather than merely avoiding defeat - is likely. With a pick ‘em 2.5 line, Overs is the strong selection.
[...]

results.title: Haiti vs Scotland Preview 06/14/2026 | Forebet
highlights:
Haiti and Scotland begin their FIFA World Cup 2026 Group C campaigns with a meeting that brings together Haiti’s recent attacking productivity and Scotland’s more measured, resilient tournament profile.
[...]
Haiti and Scotland meet at Boston Stadium in Group C of the FIFA World Cup 2026, with both sides looking for a composed start in a section where early points could shape the tone of the campaign. This is a neutral tournament fixture, so the focus falls on recent international form, scoring patterns, squad balance and how each coach is likely to approach the contest.
[...]
Haiti arrive under Sébastien Migné with strong overall numbers across their recent run. They have won 17 of their last 30 matches in all competitions, averaging 2.63 goals scored and 1.23 conceded across that spell. That attacking return is notable and suggests a side capable of creating chances through direct forward play and quick transitions.
[...]
Scotland, coached by Steve Clarke, bring a different profile. Their last 30 matches in all competitions show 15 wins, with an average of 1.63 goals scored and 1.27 conceded. Those figures are not as explosive as Haiti’s, but they reflect a side often built on structure, midfield intensity and disciplined defensive spacing.
[...]
The Scottish trend of resilience is one of the main reasons they enter this match with a slight edge. Scotland have not been defeated in 9 of their last 11 matches in all competitions (non-friendlies), while they have also won by 2 or more goals in 3 of their last 7. That combination of stability and enough cutting edge makes them difficult to break down over 90 minutes. That resilience is also why Forebet predicts Scotland to qualify for the Round of 32 as well, albeit as third in the group.
[...]
The match may not develop into an open scoring contest despite Haiti’s strong attacking averages. Scotland’s recent record suggests they are comfortable managing tight spells, and their midfield has the tools to slow Haiti’s transitions. If Clarke’s side keep their spacing compact, they can limit the number of high-quality chances Haiti generate.
[...]
Haiti have enough attacking quality to make this competitive, but Scotland’s unbeaten trend, defensive organisation and stronger probability profile make them the more likely winners. The prediction is Scotland to win with a 57% probability, with under 2.5 goals expected and a 0-2 scoreline.
